vectors.name: render-int-negative
vectors.note: A leading - when negative, no +, no leading zeros.

vectors.name: render-float-zero
vectors.note: Zero renders 0.0 -- at least one digit after the point.

vectors.name: render-float-negative-zero
vectors.note: Negative zero is preserved and rendered, so a host cannot normalise it away (ABI 6.3.1 rule 6).

vectors.name: render-float-lower-fixed-bound
vectors.note: 1e-4 is the inclusive lower edge of the fixed-point window.

vectors.name: render-float-just-below-lower-bound
vectors.note: Below 1e-4 goes scientific. The spec's own example.

vectors.name: render-float-upper-fixed-bound
vectors.note: 1e15 is inside the window; the exclusive upper edge is 1e16.

vectors.name: render-float-at-upper-bound
vectors.note: At 1e16 the rendering switches to scientific, with no digits after the point when there are none.

vectors.name: render-float-max
vectors.note: The largest finite binary64. Without the upper bound on fixed-point this would be 310 characters.

vectors.name: render-float-min-subnormal
vectors.note: The smallest positive subnormal. The shortest digit string that round-trips is one digit.

vectors.name: render-float-shortest-roundtrip
vectors.note: Shortest round-tripping decimal, not the exact binary value: 0.1 is not representable, and 0.1000000000000000055511151231257827 round-trips to the same double.

vectors.name: render-float-negative-exponent-no-plus
vectors.note: The exponent carries - when negative and never +, and never a leading zero.

vectors.name: render-string-quoted-when-nested
vectors.note: The same string is bare at the top level and quoted inside a container, so a rendered container re-reads as itself.

vectors.name: render-string-escapes
vectors.note: Quote and backslash escape when nested -- 3.1's escape set exactly.

vectors.name: render-string-low-scalar-escape
vectors.note: Any other scalar below U+0020 uses \u{h...} with lowercase hex and no leading zeros.

vectors.name: render-string-non-ascii-is-itself
vectors.note: Every other scalar renders as itself: no \u escaping of ordinary text, and no normalisation.

vectors.name: render-bytes-lowercase-hex
vectors.note: Lowercase hex, two digits per byte, no separator, unquoted at the top level.

vectors.name: render-array-separator
vectors.note: Elements in order, separated by a comma and a space.

vectors.name: render-array-mixed-types
vectors.note: int 1 and float 1.0 render differently, which is why the vector notation tags them.

vectors.name: render-map-keys-quoted-and-sorted
vectors.note: Ascending key order regardless of construction order (2), and keys are always quoted. This is what makes a rendered map the same text on every host.

vectors.name: render-map-key-order-is-bytewise
vectors.note: Bytewise over UTF-8, so uppercase sorts before lowercase -- not a locale collation.

vectors.name: render-str-concatenates-renderings
vectors.note: str renders each argument by the same rules, so 7.6 pins str's output too.

vectors.name: render-function-is-type-error
vectors.note: A function has no rendering.

vectors.name: render-field-pins-the-result-rendering
vectors.note: A vector may pin both the value and its rendering; the two assertions are independent, and this one shows the `render` field doing the job (string x) does above.
